title: Cities: Skylines | Power, Politics, & Planning: Episode 6: Public Housing Part 2
premise: donoteat01 argues that privatized housing subsidies, redevelopment incentives, demolition, and limits on collective labor investment keep housing from working as a public good. A fictional neighborhood’s dispersal leads through Boston and Philadelphia examples to his case for tenant organizing and universal public housing.
coverage: City footage, photographs, cartoons and diagrams follow housing subsidies, neighborhood displacement and alternatives to private ownership. Historical, fiscal and legal claims are the presenter’s. Brief inserts may be missed; cut times and sound-cue placement are approximate.

panels.heading: Previously: housing and clearance
panels.description: Simulated apartment towers and road infrastructure introduce the Part 1 recap.
panels.camera: High aerial gameplay views move around the city.
panels.action: Traffic is present; the named historical residents are not shown.

panels.heading: Episode title
panels.description: The blue Cities: Skylines title graphic identifies the game-based presentation.
panels.camera: Static title graphic, edited into city footage.
panels.action: No visible character action.

panels.heading: Capital versus public control
panels.description: CAPITAL ABHORS PUBLIC CONTROL / WHERE PROFIT CAN BE MADE overlays the Greenbelt aerial.
panels.camera: Static text over an aerial view.
panels.action: Words state the episode’s organizing conflict.

panels.heading: Nixon halts construction
panels.description: Futurama’s Richard Nixon head-in-a-jar character replaces a sober presidential portrait as the moratorium is explained.
panels.camera: Static cartoon insert; hard change from the housing footage.
panels.action: The head sits in its jar.
panels.visualGag: Futurama’s Nixon supplies the satirical face of the policy turn.

panels.heading: Who receives the subsidy?
panels.description: TO LANDLORDS emphasizes the private recipient of public payments.
panels.action: Caption foregrounds the funding destination.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the recipient/choice sequence: public money goes TO LANDLORDS; the following cartoon recipient and asterisk-heavy ANY BUILDING comparison undercut the voucher’s promise.

panels.heading: The Section 8 recipient
panels.description: Scruffy, the janitor from Futurama, reclines reading ZERO-G JUGGS beneath the recipient label.
panels.action: Scruffy reclines with a magazine.
panels.visualGag: The beneficiary illustration is a deliberately undignified cartoon rather than a housing-policy diagram.

panels.heading: Choice, with asterisks
panels.description: A split comparison of decaying housing and luxurious towers promises ANY BUILDING, then restricts it to participating landlords and probably the left-hand buildings.
panels.camera: Static split image and layered footnotes.
panels.action: Footnotes overturn the headline.
panels.visualGag: The second asterisk punctures the apparent promise of unrestricted choice.

panels.heading: Subsidy scale
panels.description: A funding comparison appears over the simulated city while the narrator contrasts Section 8 and conventional public housing.
panels.action: No individual people are shown.

panels.heading: Waiting lists close
panels.description: City photographs accompany a roll call of housing authorities with closed waiting lists.
panels.action: No applicant is individually shown.

panels.heading: Nixon correction
panels.description: Futurama’s angry Richard Nixon head in a jar appears beside a headless suit, with DAMN HIPPIES! and the correction * HE RESIGNED.
panels.action: The caption corrects the spoken description.
panels.visualGag: The cartoon interruption also catches the narrator’s impeachment wording.

panels.heading: Community development grants
panels.description: The game city supports the explanation of 1974 grants for infrastructure and economic development.
panels.camera: Aerial viewpoints change from shot to shot.
panels.action: City buildings and roads stand in for the institutions receiving money.

panels.heading: Outsourcing public responsibility
panels.description: Neoliberalism and landlord-oriented captions accompany ordinary city blocks.
panels.camera: Text overlays on gameplay as the camera view changes.
panels.action: No visible individual landlord is identified.

panels.heading: Acquisition without repair
panels.description: An isolated deteriorating rowhouse illustrates scattered-site housing left to decay.
panels.action: Building condition is visible; deterioration itself is not filmed in progress.
panels.visualGag: Played straight: the decaying house, bought but never repaired, sets up the conspiracy-wall and jargon sequence that follows.

panels.heading: Policy as conspiracy wall
panels.description: Charlie Kelly (Charlie Day) from It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia gestures at the Pepe Silvia conspiracy wall, introducing the deliberately overcomplicated policy example.
panels.action: A photographed character gestures amid strings and papers.
panels.visualGag: The meme makes the policy’s elaborate connections look absurd.

panels.heading: The jargon overwhelms the frame
panels.description: Policy terminology accumulates around a large CLIMATE CHANGE label.
panels.camera: Successive static typography slides grow more crowded.
panels.action: On-screen words accumulate; no human action.
panels.visualGag: Unreadable-looking policy clutter is the visual counterpart to the invented mechanism.

panels.heading: Socialists disagree
panels.description: A Soviet flag photograph carries SOCIALISTS DISAGREE.
panels.action: The pictured flag-raising is historical-image content, not present-day footage.
panels.visualGag: A blunt ideological response contrasts with the preceding policy tangle.

panels.heading: An inscrutable contract
panels.description: Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory presents the ornate contract and quill, with Gene Wilder as Willy Wonka.
panels.action: Characters are pictured at the contract.
panels.visualGag: LIHTC’s complexity is analogized to an absurdly elaborate contract.

panels.heading: A soothing explanation?
panels.description: A North Korean military parade begins beneath the tax-credit explanation.
panels.camera: Edited parade footage replaces the housing imagery and cuts between parade views.
panels.action: Troops march in formation.
panels.visualGag: The promised “soothing footage” for the LIHTC explanation turns out to be a North Korean military parade set to the North Korean national anthem. Martial music under a reassuring walkthrough of tax credits is the satirical joke.

sound.text: The North Korean national anthem plays under the parade as the LIHTC explanation gets going.

panels.heading: Credits, allocations, middlemen
panels.description: Parade leaders and massed formations continue while the narration explains allocations, developer bids, investors, and eligibility.
panels.action: Leaders and formations remain the visual subjects rather than housing applicants.
panels.visualGag: The parade mismatch persists through the complicated mechanism, extending the earlier joke.

panels.heading: Parade payoff
panels.description: Military vehicles and aircraft continue the prolonged diversion from affordable housing.
panels.camera: Edited parade sequence with wide framing.
panels.action: Vehicles and formations change between views.
panels.visualGag: A long visual detour undercuts the bureaucratic promise of a simple explanation.

panels.heading: With extra steps
panels.description: Rick and Morty’s SLAVERY WITH EXTRA STEPS reaction follows the complicated subsidy account.
panels.action: A still image.
panels.visualGag: A familiar reaction phrase compresses the long mechanism into a joke.

panels.heading: You are right
panels.description: YOU’RE RIGHT follows the reaction image.
panels.action: Text explicitly endorses the preceding comparison.
panels.visualGag: The card is the on-screen payoff to the extra-steps gag, and the inside-out cow that follows illustrates the next sentence literally.

panels.heading: Backwards and inside out
panels.description: A blue 3D cow is stretched inside out between wooden beams after the YOU’RE RIGHT card. The animation’s source is unknown.
panels.action: The cow’s distorted body hangs between the supports.
panels.visualGag: The inside-out cow pays off the description of the subsidy as backwards and inside out, closing the EXTRA STEPS / YOU’RE RIGHT exchange.

panels.heading: Sacks of cash
panels.description: A stock-product image of a dollar-sign bag illustrates direct cash subsidies.
panels.action: No character action; the bag is a pictured object.
panels.visualGag: The sack-of-cash metaphor becomes an actual commercial money-bag photograph.

panels.heading: HOPE VI arrives
panels.description: Program text and housing imagery introduce replacement of concentrated poverty with mixed-income development.
panels.camera: Static explanatory graphics intercut with city footage.
panels.action: No identified resident action.

panels.heading: New Urbanism, same rendering
panels.description: A development rendering receives design-category captions.
panels.camera: Static rendering reused with changing labels.
panels.action: The built proposal is illustrated, not shown being constructed.

panels.heading: Cuomo and the MTA
panels.description: Cuomo’s portrait carries the parenthetical WHO NOW CONTROLS THE MTA.
panels.action: No character action.
panels.visualGag: An unspoken transit aside intrudes into the HUD discussion.

panels.heading: Severely distressed?
panels.description: The game project and explanatory caption establish the looseness of the redevelopment category.
panels.camera: Aerial views of the city change framing.
panels.action: The towers remain standing at this stage.

panels.heading: A valuable 52nd Street site
panels.description: Towers beside major infrastructure provide the fictional redevelopment setting.
panels.camera: Aerial viewpoints circle and reframe the project.
panels.action: Traffic moves through the surrounding network.

panels.heading: Meet the developer
panels.description: The Realty Partners for Progress logo appears over the simulated project, introducing the named fictional developer before the actual office-building photograph in the next panel.
panels.camera: Static logo overlay on the game aerial, which crossfades to a building photograph in the next panel.
panels.action: No developer meeting is visibly acted out.
panels.visualGag: The polished developer logo gives way to a bland Delaware office, then to the mock architect credit and happy stock-people rendering.

panels.heading: The headquarters: 1209 North Orange Street
panels.description: A beige office building stands behind sidewalk trees. A burgundy awning reads 1209, and white text gives 1209 N ORANGE STREET, WILMINGTON, DE.
panels.camera: The developer logo crossfades into a static street-level building photograph and address caption.
panels.action: No people appear; the photograph and address caption replace the polished developer logo.
panels.visualGag: A bland office building undercuts the impressive developer branding before the glossy brochure arrives.
panels.notes: The caption and narration supply the address; the photograph itself shows no wrongdoing.

panels.heading: Professional brochure, joke architect
panels.description: The 52nd Street Commons Mixed-Income Housing rendering credits dewey bildem + howe architects.
panels.action: No character action.
panels.visualGag: The respectable-looking architect credit hides a construction-name sound-alike joke.

panels.heading: The entourage
panels.description: A publicity image of the Entourage television cast accompanies the developer entourage.
panels.action: The men pose together in a still photograph.
panels.visualGag: The Entourage cast literalizes the developer entourage; the publicity photograph’s origin is unknown.

panels.heading: Future residents as cutouts
panels.description: A real rendering is marked HAPPY CUT-OUT (WHITE) PEOPLE with red circles and arrows.
panels.action: Annotations identify stock figures, not actual tenants.
panels.visualGag: Idealized white future residents expose the exclusion implicit in redevelopment imagery.

panels.heading: Stock people behind the optimism
panels.description: Cutout-people resource websites show the supply of figures used in renderings.
panels.action: Visible website pages offer cutout figures.
panels.visualGag: The follow-up exposes the artificial machinery behind the happy-rendering promise.

panels.heading: Professional demolition meets spectacle
panels.description: Large simulated explosions strike the project towers.
panels.camera: Wide aerial game view as the demolition effects change rapidly.
panels.action: Explosions and smoke engulf buildings.
panels.visualGag: Destructive game spectacle contradicts the language of controlled, professional redevelopment.

panels.heading: The redevelopment crater
panels.description: A vast blackened hole, flames, and smoke occupy the project site.
panels.action: Fire and smoke continue after the towers are destroyed.
panels.visualGag: The demolition gag pays off as a ruin rather than an orderly cleared parcel.

panels.heading: An eviction policy in plain writing
panels.description: A Saint John redevelopment billboard explains relocation for existing tenants and no help for newcomers.
panels.action: No tenant relocation is filmed.

panels.heading: The Mikes lose a neighborhood
panels.description: The game neighborhood illustrates the narrated family, hardware store, and local relationships.
panels.action: None of the game’s citizens can be picked out as a Mike.

panels.heading: Floor M
panels.description: An elevator-button photograph shows B, M, and 1.
panels.action: No elevator ride or named resident is visible.
panels.visualGag: The literal mezzanine button supplies the floor-M misdirection’s visual payoff.

panels.heading: Dispersal instead of reunion
panels.description: Rail-side apartments and more distant housing landscapes accompany the family’s separation.
panels.camera: Edited changes of game location and aerial framing.
panels.action: Buildings represent destinations; Michelle is not individually depicted.

panels.heading: The replacement neighborhood
panels.description: New low- and mid-rise buildings and retail replace the old tower setting.
panels.action: Traffic and city activity continue; displaced residents are not tracked on screen.

panels.heading: Maverick Landing sells itself
panels.description: Boston apartment websites and waterfront imagery introduce the real redevelopment example.
panels.camera: Static website captures and changing aerial scale.
panels.action: No actual housing applicant is filmed.

panels.heading: Before and after Maverick
panels.description: Dated archival aerials show the changing footprint of Maverick housing.
panels.camera: Cuts between dated aerial images, with zooming and reframing.
panels.action: Buildings disappear or change between historical images, not within live construction footage.

panels.heading: Prime land, fewer public homes
panels.description: Waterfront and transit geography support the presenter’s displacement and replacement-count argument.
panels.camera: The oblique aerial view shifts from shot to shot.
panels.action: No individual resident action.

panels.heading: Richard Allen changes form
panels.description: Older dense rowhousing and later suburban-style development are contrasted.
panels.camera: Cuts between archival aerials and modern views.
panels.action: Changes in housing form are shown as before/after images.

panels.heading: Sharswood is planned
panels.description: Maps, marked-up parcels, and acquisition reporting establish the Philadelphia redevelopment program.
panels.camera: Static maps and reporting screenshots, edited in succession.
panels.action: Highlighted areas identify proposals; no acquisition transaction is filmed.

panels.heading: Institutional headquarters
panels.description: A headquarters rendering and local streets juxtapose administrative investment with the neighborhood.
panels.camera: Cuts among rendering and street images.
panels.action: No construction is shown.

panels.heading: Blumberg towers fall
panels.description: Photographic demolition footage shows dust at the tower site.
panels.camera: Wide view of the demolition as the dust spreads.
panels.action: The towers implode and the dust cloud grows.

panels.heading: Oxford Street’s date caveat
panels.description: Street View is explicitly dated 2009 with the qualification that the narrator saw it looking similar in 2014.
panels.camera: Static street image with correction text.
panels.action: No character action.

panels.heading: An exposed party wall
panels.description: A surviving house exposes the side wall left by an adjacent demolition.
panels.action: Damage/exposure is pictured; rain damage is explained by speech rather than filmed.

panels.heading: Demolition by neglect
panels.description: Successive street images end with missing houses and a diminished block.
panels.camera: Edited before/after photographs; no continuous camera movement.
panels.action: Buildings are absent in later images.
panels.visualGag: Played straight, the image sequence shows the cumulative loss.

panels.heading: North Philly Peace Park
panels.description: A welcome sign and garden establish the community-created green space.
panels.action: No gardener is individually tracked.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the connected pie-attraction gag: this real community garden is narrated as a cartoon pie on a windowsill; the following Yogi Bear and Mickey inserts supply the literal payoff.

panels.heading: Drawn to the pie
panels.description: Hanna-Barbera’s Yogi Bear cartoon imagery interrupts the garden account.
panels.camera: Cartoon insert; the poses change as Yogi goes after the food.
panels.action: Cartoon character is attracted to food.
panels.visualGag: The developer attraction-to-land metaphor is literalized by a pie-seeking cartoon.

panels.heading: Another aroma follower
panels.description: Disney’s Mickey Mouse follows the cartoon-aroma motif toward a window.
panels.action: Mickey is pictured drawn by the aroma.
panels.visualGag: A second cartoon extends the pie metaphor rather than adding a documentary housing claim.

panels.heading: The garden is moved
panels.description: Street views of houses and the replacement garden follow the displacement account.
panels.camera: Static location images change by cuts.
panels.action: The plants are not shown being moved.

panels.heading: The narrator’s own survey work
panels.description: Street imagery accompanies the admission of inaccurate windshield surveys.
panels.camera: Street-view sequence with changing vantage points.
panels.action: No identified intern or narrator is visibly inside a car.

panels.heading: Public plans that are hard to read
panels.description: The housing authority website’s plans/maps area leads to small and pixelated map displays.
panels.camera: The website is navigated and its map enlarged.
panels.action: Pages and map scale change.
panels.visualGag: Whether or not it is meant as a joke, the unreadable maps undercut the promise of public information.

panels.heading: Occupy PHA’s demands
panels.description: Protest signs and a written demand document put land reuse, rehabilitation, and accountability on screen.
panels.camera: Static signs, then the document scrolls.
panels.action: Text position changes as the document is navigated.

panels.heading: The backhoe allegation
panels.description: A narrow phone-video view shows machinery, bucket, and cab during the protest discussion.
panels.camera: Vertical phone-video inset; limited field of view.
panels.action: The machinery is visible; the footage itself does not show the alleged attempt to run protesters over.

panels.heading: PHIMBYs
panels.description: PUBLIC HOUSING IN MY BACK YARD joins the familiar housing-policy acronyms.
panels.action: Labels define the category.
panels.visualGag: A new acronym repurposes the YIMBY/NIMBY vocabulary for public housing.

panels.heading: More than Bernie
panels.description: A muscular, colorful Bernie Sanders cartoon accompanies the call for more ambitious action.
panels.action: No documentary politician action.
panels.visualGag: The exaggerated, muscular Bernie caricature leads into the Republican elephant and Democratic donkey pairing.

panels.heading: Half of Congress: the elephant
panels.description: A large red-and-blue Republican elephant replaces the muscular Bernie illustration over the game city.
panels.camera: Bernie crossfades into the static Republican elephant logo.
panels.action: The party symbol replaces the caricature; no character motion.
panels.visualGag: First half of a connected partisan pairing: the elephant illustrates the claim that half of Congress actively wants public housing to fail; the donkey follows for the other half.
panels.notes: The party-symbol comparison expresses the presenter’s political argument.

panels.heading: The other half: the donkey
panels.description: A red-and-blue Democratic donkey replaces the Republican elephant over city gameplay.
panels.camera: The elephant crossfades into the Democratic donkey logo.
panels.action: One symbol replaces the other.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the half-and-half comparison: the Democratic donkey accompanies ambivalence, contrasted with the preceding Republican elephant and failure claim.

panels.heading: Billionaire alternatives
panels.description: Musk with a conspicuously large cigarette and Kanye in an oversized suit appear in a collage.
panels.action: The images exaggerate the size of the clothing and the cigarette.
panels.visualGag: Comic celebrity imagery punctures the turn to celebrity housing solutions.

panels.heading: Construction is not land
panels.description: Concrete housing imagery and conventional houses accompany the distinction between building cost and land cost.
panels.action: No actual low-cost production line is shown.

panels.heading: A tiny house still needs a site
panels.description: A tiny house on a trailer makes the land-use objection concrete.
panels.action: No towing or siting action is visible.

panels.heading: Historical alternatives
panels.description: Modernist housing imagery supports the discussion of city and union development in Weimar Germany.
panels.action: No historical figures appear.

panels.heading: Community land trusts
panels.description: The WCRP website supplies a concrete organization for the alternative-ownership argument.
panels.action: No meeting of trust members is visible.

panels.heading: Free money?
panels.description: Matthew Lesko’s question-mark suit and FREE MONEY book appear during the funding discussion.
panels.action: He is pictured holding the book.
panels.visualGag: The government-support problem gets a conspicuously literal free-money salesman image.

panels.heading: Labor built housing
panels.description: City footage bridges into Co-op City, union resources, and the historical funding question.
panels.camera: Successive aerial reframing of the game city.
panels.action: No historical union construction is directly filmed.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the pension war-chest and veto cartoons: the labor-funded-housing problem leads directly to Mr. Krabs treasure and employer top-hat refusals. The game city itself is not the joke.

panels.heading: The union war chest
panels.description: Mr. Krabs from SpongeBob SquarePants appears with a treasure chest before the pension-governance argument.
panels.action: Character is pictured beside treasure.
panels.visualGag: The financial war-chest metaphor becomes cartoon treasure.

panels.heading: Employer veto
panels.description: Conference-table stick figures and top hats respond NO! to spending on strikers.
panels.camera: The static diagram changes state between cuts.
panels.action: Captioned proposals and answers replace acted dialogue.
panels.visualGag: Employer control is reduced to a blunt veto in the cartoon boardroom.

panels.heading: The veto extends to ownership
panels.description: BUY SHARES OF COMPANY receives another NO!; employer hats change colors in the multi-employer variation.
panels.camera: Diagram changes rather than a camera move.
panels.action: Labels and hat colors change.
panels.visualGag: Repeating the veto exposes the limitation; colored employers make the institutional variation visible.

panels.heading: Meet the fiduciary
panels.description: The stonks meme figure is labeled THE FIDUCIARY.
panels.action: The figure doesn’t move.
panels.visualGag: A market meme caricatures the solemn duty to maximize returns.

panels.heading: Option A: housing
panels.description: Social-housing imagery establishes the low-return investment in the simplified comparison.
panels.action: No investment transaction is filmed.
panels.visualGag: Straight setup within the three-option investment joke: socially useful housing has low returns; the later literal Dick portraits reveal the supposedly superior app investment.

panels.heading: Option B: a company stake
panels.description: A Standard Oil share certificate represents the company-investment alternative.
panels.action: No purchasing of shares is directly shown.
panels.visualGag: Second straight setup in the investment joke: a share certificate represents worker company ownership before the three-Dicks app reveal and employer return-maximization payoff.

panels.heading: Option C: three Richards
panels.description: Portraits labeled Richard Nixon, Richard Branson, and Richard Hammond illustrate the proposed dick-pic app.
panels.action: No explicit sexual imagery or app demonstration.
panels.visualGag: Dick pics are pictures of men named Richard: the literal-name reveal is the payoff.

panels.heading: The employer chooses returns
panels.description: Mr. Krabs from SpongeBob SquarePants in a pile of money is labeled THE EMPLOYER.
panels.action: Character is pictured among cash.
panels.visualGag: The money-loving employer caricature answers the investment-choice setup.

panels.heading: A real ownership limitation
panels.description: GM board reporting illustrates the difficulty of converting worker investment into control.
panels.camera: Static news screenshots change by cuts.
panels.action: No board meeting is filmed.
panels.visualGag: This documentary bridge is not itself a joke: the limit on company ownership rules out option B and leads back to SOCIAL HOUSING OR DICK PIC APP? and the repeated Richard portraits.

panels.heading: Housing or the app?
panels.description: The comparison asks SOCIAL HOUSING OR DICK PIC APP?
panels.action: The alternatives are written on screen.
panels.visualGag: The text resets the investment joke for a callback.

panels.heading: The Richards return
panels.description: The three named Richards reappear after the choice question.
panels.action: No character action.
panels.visualGag: The repeated literal Dick portraits complete the investment example’s recurring visual joke.

sound.text: “Fonds de solidarité” gets a poor French pronunciation as the Quebec fund is introduced.

panels.heading: Quebec’s solidarity fund
panels.description: Fonds de solidarité branding introduces the FTQ fund; the presenter isn’t sure whether it plays any role in housing.
panels.action: No fund investment is visibly carried out.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the French-language aside: Fonds de solidarité and FTQ branding introduce another Francophone example; the next logo panel asks why there is so much French in the series.

sound.text: The Quebec union’s name also gets a poor French pronunciation. The caption gives it in full as Fédération des travailleurs et travailleuses du Québec.

panels.heading: Why so much French?
panels.description: FTQ branding and the expanded French union name receive the parenthetical language complaint.
panels.action: The aside is printed, not spoken.
panels.visualGag: An unspoken callback notices how often Francophone examples enter the series.

panels.heading: Individual retirement atomizes power
panels.description: The game city accompanies the move from collective funds to individual retirement and asset-manager holdings.
panels.action: No individual saver is pictured.
panels.visualGag: Played straight, the shift to individual tax-advantaged retirement accounts sets up the 401(k)/IRA acronym gag and its brief masked-paramilitary insert.

panels.heading: Retirement vehicles: 401(k) setup
panels.description: A large 401(k) caption appears over the simulated rowhouse neighborhood as individual retirement vehicles are discussed.
panels.camera: Static caption over gameplay as the game viewpoint changes.
panels.action: The account label overlays the city; no individual retirement transaction is filmed.
panels.visualGag: Straight labeled setup for the connected IRA acronym pun: the next panel swaps financial terminology for a masked armed-group photograph at the spoken IRAs.

panels.heading: IRAs: the masked-men payoff
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph of masked men holding long guns overlays the game city beside the still-visible 401(k) caption.
panels.action: The photograph shows the armed men walking.
panels.visualGag: At “IRAs,” the retirement-account acronym turns into an apparent Irish Republican Army pun, with the masked gunmen as the literal other meaning after the 401(k) label.
panels.notes: Where the photograph comes from, and exactly which armed group it shows, is unknown.

panels.heading: A rock and a hard place
panels.description: Homer Simpson from The Simpsons hangs between a rock and a building labeled A HARD PLACE.
panels.action: Homer hangs in place.
panels.visualGag: The institutional dilemma becomes a literal familiar idiom.

panels.heading: The ruined-city reprise
panels.description: Explosion aftermath and the damaged simulated city return after the constrained-options discussion.
panels.action: Fire and smoke remain visible.
panels.visualGag: The earlier redevelopment catastrophe returns, apparently to illustrate the dead end.

panels.heading: A small Queens proposal, a huge queue
panels.description: A building rendering follows reporting on the Queens project; the wait-list scale contrasts with its modest supply.
panels.camera: Static news and rendering inserts followed by game imagery.
panels.action: No construction of the proposed units is visibly filmed.

panels.heading: Tenant organizing now
panels.description: Burning and congested game streets continue beneath tenant-union, rent-control, and just-cause proposals.
panels.camera: Changing street and aerial viewpoints in the game.
panels.action: Emergency vehicles and traffic are visible; named tenants are not depicted.

panels.heading: Build and protect
panels.description: The ongoing game city supports the refusal to choose between more apartments and anti-displacement protections.
panels.action: City vehicles continue through the streets.

panels.heading: A longer-term horizon
panels.description: The city remains damaged as the narrator widens the reforms beyond zoning to work itself.
panels.camera: Gameplay views alternate scale and position.
panels.action: Fires and traffic persist.
panels.visualGag: The fires make a visible contrast with the reform proposals, though it is unclear whether they are timed to particular sentences.

panels.heading: Universal public housing
panels.description: Broad city views accompany rapid building, acquisition without displacement, and housing for all incomes.
panels.camera: Wider aerial game framing through the sequence.
panels.action: No completed universal program is enacted in the footage.

panels.heading: Everyone except landlords
panels.description: The affirmative conclusion returns to Red Vienna and broad benefit with landlords excepted.
panels.camera: Changing game-city views accompany the conclusion.
panels.action: No landlord character is individually shown.
panels.visualGag: The closing joke is spoken over ordinary game footage: everyone benefits, except the landlords. No landlord or reaction image appears.

panels.heading: An actual Twitter complaint
panels.description: A screenshot displays a Patreon-versus-output complaint while the outro invites criticism.
panels.action: Nobody is shown typing.
panels.visualGag: The invitation to complain is backed by an already-existing complaint as a visual receipt.

panels.heading: The supporter pitch
panels.description: Game footage accompanies Franklin, Killdozer, coffee-money, piracy-economics, and advertising remarks.
panels.action: No supporter transaction is shown.

panels.heading: My Patreons
panels.description: White contributor names in columns appear on black beneath the credits heading.
panels.camera: Credits scroll vertically through the sequence.
panels.action: Text moves upward; no visible characters.

panels.heading: Credits continue
panels.description: More contributor names pass through the black credit field.
panels.action: Successive names enter and leave the frame.

panels.heading: One fare: closing token
panels.description: A silver circular token with a red stripe reads GOOD FOR / DNE / ONE FARE.
panels.action: No character action and no further speech.
